model_notes.nodes: post-shift states only; every node has L2 = empty
model_notes.edge: fill slot 0 to full via first-empty branching over bottom-anchored templates, then shift

gate_theorem.statement: A state P is a predecessor of state 0 iff P has L1 = L2 = empty AND the complement of P.L0 (a*b - |P.L0| cells) is exactly coverable by flat T orientations (z-span = 1).
gate_theorem.necessity_proof_sketch: Monotonicity forces P.L1 empty; every template used must avoid slots 1 and 2; T orientation profiles are {(5,0,0)x4, (1,3,1)x4, (3,1,1)x2, (1,1,3)x2}, so every non-flat placement meets slot 1; hence only flat orientations were used and they exactly cover the complement.
gate_theorem.sufficiency_proof_sketch: First-empty branching is complete for exact cover; a flat cover of the complement fills to (FULL, empty, empty), whose shift is 0.
gate_theorem.degenerate_cases: P.L0 full: empty cover, direct shift edge to 0. P = 0: requires whole-layer rectangle tiling by T pentominoes (none exists at tested sizes).

sufficiency.claim: 5 | (a*b - |P.L0|) together with L1 = L2 = empty implies P -> 0.

counterexample.detail: No flat T placement fits (flat bounding boxes are 3x3); no subset of size divisible by 5 is flat-coverable; complete closure finds no predecessor of 0 (graph has no complete fill at all), yet P = 0 is reachable with 5 | (10 - 0).

sufficiency.correct_condition: exact coverability of comp(P.L0) by flat T orientations

first_generation_sufficiency_for_finding.claim: First-generation BFS suffices to find all predecessors of 0.
first_generation_sufficiency_for_finding.why_false: Macro nodes are post-shift states (X, Y, empty). A fill from a parent with Y non-empty that avoids the parent's slot 2 (span <= 2 pieces) yields a child (X', empty, empty). Hence L1=L2=empty nodes occur behind ancestors with non-empty L1 at unbounded depth.
first_generation_sufficiency_for_finding.demonstration: On 3x7, all 204 generation-1 sources have Y non-empty (zero L1=L2=empty depth-1 nodes), yet the completed closure contains two predecessors of 0 (both |L0|=11): both sit at depth >= 2.
first_generation_sufficiency_for_finding.consequence: Acyclic conclusions require full closure; no fixed-depth truncation decides the question.

cyclicity_criterion.statement: The T axb Macro graph admits a closed walk through state 0 iff some reachable node P has L1 = L2 = empty and comp(P.L0) exactly coverable by flat T orientations.
cyclicity_criterion.derived_from: gate theorem + definition of closed walk
cyclicity_criterion.decision_procedure: Breadth-first Macro closure from state 0 with early constructive exit on a gate-satisfying node; ACYCLIC only on uncapped completion.
cyclicity_criterion.cost_note: Same order as full closure; there is no known cheaper complete test. First-generation cost tables are not evidence of completeness.
